answer: Sybil farms thrive when a thousand names share one machine, so make storage the price of a name. The network keeps a large public dataset, the Nebula file, and each identity must hold its own copy re-encoded with its public key, so copies cannot be shared. Random spot checks ask for pieces, such as one from a given grove of blocks, within a few seconds. The attacker must buy and power a separate copper-wired disk for every fake, and a miss loses the name.
